tip.en: Pace slowed to ~8:20 yet HR jumped from 106 to 122 in under 20 seconds — a classic sign of a standing start catching up with you. Your recent runs avg 136 bpm at much longer distances; this cardiac cost so early in a 3.6 km outing signals your warm-up was too abrupt.
tip.zh: 配速降到约8:20，但心率在不到20秒内从106飙升至122——这是启动过猛、身体滞后响应的典型信号。对比近期跑步平均136bpm却跑更长距离，说明今天热身衔接过于仓促。

tip.en: HR reaches 154–155 at km 1.0 while pace is only 7:00–7:15 — an unusually high cardiac cost for such easy running. Compare this to your 5 km runs where 155 bpm powered sub-6:00 pace; here the same heart rate buys you little speed, hinting at residual fatigue or a very cold start to this midday effort.
tip.zh: 1公里处心率攀升至154-155，而配速仅7:00–7:15——以如此轻松的速度换来这么高的心脏负荷，实属异常。对比近期5公里跑中155bpm能维持破6分配速，今天同等心率却换不来速度，提示可能存在疲劳积累或热身不足。

tip.en: Pace collapses to 26:00 and position freezes for over two minutes — almost certainly a red light or pedestrian crossing. HR drops from 151 to 116 in that window, a 35-beat recovery that will inflate your average HR calculation and distort any training load estimate.
tip.zh: 配速骤降至26:00，位置停滞超过两分钟——几乎可以确定是遇到了红灯或人行横道。心率在此期间从151降至116，下降35次，这会拉低平均心率并扭曲训练负荷的评估。

tip.en: After ~2 min 20 sec stationary, you re-engage at a tidy 4:59 pace within two steps — good instinct to roll back into rhythm rather than hesitate. HR is only 100 bpm at this point, so you have a large aerobic buffer to rebuild effort gradually.
tip.zh: 停止约2分20秒后，你仅用两步就以4:59的配速重新投入跑步——这种不犹豫、直接找回节奏的本能很好。此时心率仅100bpm，有充足的有氧空间逐步加载强度。

title.en: Second Dead Stop — Longer This Time

tip.en: Another standstill lasting nearly 90 seconds at km 2.6, with HR dropping from 148 all the way to 100 — a 48-beat crash. Two enforced stops totalling ~4 minutes in a 20-minute run means roughly 20% of your moving time was lost to road crossings; consider a route with underpasses or timed light crossings.
tip.zh: 2.6公里处再次停止约90秒，心率从148一路跌至100——下降了48次。两次强制停步合计约4分钟，占20分钟运动时间的约20%；建议选择有地下通道或红绿灯可预判的路线。

tip.en: A brief 3:13 split appears as you accelerate out of the second stop, HR still only 103 — your legs clearly had more in them than the pedestrian-pace sections suggested. Channelling this responsive fast-twitch energy into a planned fartlek mid-run would add quality without the cardiac spike you experienced earlier.
tip.zh: 第二次停步后加速时出现了3:13的瞬间配速，而此时心率仅103——你的腿显然比之前那些漫步节奏所表现出的更有弹性。若能将这种快速反应能力融入有计划的法特莱克训练，就能在不引发早段心率骤升的情况下提升训练质量。

tip.en: Grade spikes to 3.1% and pace immediately softens to 6:10 — this is the approach to what appears to be a pedestrian underpass. HR is a controlled 147, but the transition from flat road to sudden incline with cold legs is exactly where calf or Achilles strain accumulates over repeated runs on this route.
tip.zh: 坡度突然升至3.1%，配速立即放缓至6:10——这是进入人行地下通道的坡道。心率尚在可控的147，但从平路突然进入坡道，腿部肌肉尚未充分激活，这种情况反复发生正是小腿和跟腱累积劳损的高发时机。

tip.en: Grade hits -14.8% — by far the steepest terrain of the run — matching a staircase descent inside the underpass. The GPS is measuring stair-steps, not running surface; quad eccentric load here is high despite the low speed. If this is a daily route, factor in cumulative knee stress even though it appears brief.
tip.zh: 坡度达到-14.8%，是全程最陡的地形，对应地下通道内的楼梯下行。GPS记录的是阶梯高度变化，而非奔跑地面；尽管速度不快，大腿股四头肌的离心负荷仍然很高。如果这是日常路线，即便下坡段短暂，也需关注膝关节的累积压力。

title.zh: 地形起伏剧烈，心率已悄然漂移

tip.en: Between km 3.1–3.3 grade swings from +3.6% to -8.2% within a few hundred metres, suggesting a bridge or overpass structure. HR is drifting back up to 140–142 on a body that just recovered through two stops; these hidden elevation changes add more physiological load than the flat-course avg of 7 m gain implies.
tip.zh: 3.1–3.3公里段内坡度在+3.6%到-8.2%之间剧烈震荡，可能对应一座天桥或立交结构。经过两次停步恢复后，心率正在重新爬回140–142；这些隐性高度变化带来的生理负荷，远比全程7米爬升的数据所显示的要大。

tip.en: Grade peaks at 9.5% and you're climbing what looks like a second staircase ascent, yet HR is only 122 and falling — the two prolonged stops have let your cardiovascular system cool so much that even a steep stair climb barely registers. This confirms the stops, not the terrain, are driving today's HR story.
tip.zh: 坡度达到9.5%，正在攀登疑似第二处楼梯，但心率仅122且仍在下降——两次长时间停步已让心血管系统充分冷却，以至于连陡峭楼梯都几乎引不起明显心率反应。这证明今天心率走势的主角是停步，而非地形。
